name: Dham
description: Himachal's festive vegetarian feast served for weddings, birthdays and festivals, once offered only in temples. It is cooked by hereditary Brahmin chefs called botis in copper or brass vessels, without onion or garlic, and served in courses of rice, dal, madra, kadhi, rajma, khatta and a sweet; Chamba, Kangra and Mandi each have their own version.
how_to_eat: Sit on the floor and eat with your hand from the leaf plate as each course is served.
how_to_order: It is served at weddings and fairs rather than sold; some restaurants offer a 'Himachali dham' thali.

name: Madra
description: Chickpeas or kidney beans slow-cooked in a yogurt gravy with cardamom, cinnamon and cloves, usually in brass vessels. It is the highlight of the dham and is associated with Chamba; variants include kala chana madra and rajma madra.
how_to_eat: Eat it with rice, or with babru as a snack.
how_to_order: Ask for 'chana madra' at Himachali restaurants and dhabas.

name: Siddu
description: Steamed bread of fermented wheat dough stuffed with a savoury or sweet filling such as lentil paste, poppy seeds or walnuts. It is eaten in Mandi, Kullu, Manali, Rohru and Shimla.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot with desi ghee, dal or green mint chutney.
how_to_order: Ask for 'siddu with ghee' at local eateries and roadside stalls in Kullu and Manali.

name: Babru
description: A Himachali kachori: wheat flour flatbread stuffed with a paste of black gram soaked overnight, then deep-fried. It is a cold-weather evening snack.
how_to_eat: Eat it with tea and tamarind chutney, or with chana madra.
how_to_order: Ask for 'babru' at sweet shops and tea stalls, mainly in Shimla and the hills.

name: Chha Gosht
description: Lamb or mutton marinated for hours and cooked in a gravy of yogurt, gram flour and spices. It is one of the best-known non-vegetarian Himachali dishes.
how_to_eat: Eat it with rice or roti.
how_to_order: Ask for 'chha gosht' at Himachali restaurants in Shimla or Dharamshala.

name: Tudkiya Bhath
description: A spiced rice dish, similar to a pulao, cooked with potatoes, onion, garlic, ginger, cardamom, cinnamon and bay leaves. Sources link it to Chamba.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot, often with a squeeze of lemon or with madra.
how_to_order: Ask for 'tudkiya bhath' at Himachali restaurants.

name: Patrodu
description: Colocasia (taro) leaves coated in a spiced gram flour batter, rolled, steamed and sliced. Wikipedia notes the dish originated in Himachal Pradesh before spreading south.
how_to_eat: Eat the slices as a snack, plain or shallow-fried.
how_to_order: Mostly home-cooked in the monsoon; some Himachali eateries serve it.

name: Aktori
description: A pancake-like dish of buckwheat leaves, wheat flour, milk and sugar, made at festivals. The authentic version is found in Spiti and Lahaul.
how_to_eat: Eat it drizzled with ghee or honey.
how_to_order: Look for it at local eateries in Spiti and Lahaul, especially around festivals.

name: Mittha
description: Sweet rice cooked with jaggery or sugar, raisins and dry fruits. It is the sweet course of the Himachali dham.
how_to_eat: Eat it at the end of the meal.
how_to_order: Served at dhams; some Himachali restaurants offer it as a dessert.

name: Sepu Vadi
description: Steamed and fried urad dal dumplings in a spinach and yogurt gravy, traditionally cooked in mustard oil. It is a Mandi speciality and received a GI tag as 'Sepu Vadi of Mandi'.
how_to_eat: Eat it with rice or roti.
how_to_order: Ask for 'sepu vadi' at restaurants in Mandi or at a Mandyali dham.

name: Teliya Mah
description: A tangy preparation of urad dal cooked with tamarind and spices. It is one of the courses of the dham.
how_to_eat: Eat it with rice.
how_to_order: Served at dhams; ask for it in Himachali thali places.

name: Mash Dal
description: Black lentils (kali dal) soaked overnight, cooked and added to onions fried with garlic, ginger and spices. It is a Himachali speciality and part of the dham.
how_to_eat: Eat it with rice or roti.
how_to_order: Ask for 'mash dal' or 'kali dal' at Himachali restaurants.

name: Khatta
description: A sour dish made with dried mango powder or tamarind, jaggery and spices, often with chickpeas or pumpkin. It is a course of the dham.
how_to_eat: Eat it with rice in small portions.
how_to_order: Served at dhams.

name: Bhey
description: Lotus stems sliced thin and fried with onion, garlic, ginger and spices. It is eaten as an evening snack or with rice at lunch.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot as a snack or as a side with rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'bhey' at Himachali restaurants.

name: Kullu Trout
description: Trout from the cold rivers of the Kullu valley, marinated with minimal spices and cooked to keep its natural taste. Trout from Kullu-Manali, Barot, Sangla and Pabbar valleys is a regional speciality.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot with lemon, often with rice or salad.
how_to_order: Ask for 'trout fish' at restaurants in Kullu and Manali.

name: Khatta Karai Meat
description: A sour-spicy meat curry that is popular in Kangra and parts of Mandi. The state tourism department lists it among Himachal's well-known local dishes.
how_to_eat: Eat it with rice or roti.
how_to_order: Ask for it at local non-veg eateries in Kangra.

name: Chamba Chukh
description: A cooked chilli sauce of sun-dried red or fresh green chillies blended with citrus from a local fruit, made by women at home in Chamba. It is a generations-old preparation now sold more widely; its GI application is pending.
how_to_eat: Use a small amount as a relish with rice, dal or snacks.
how_to_order: Buy bottled chukh in Chamba markets.

name: Kangra Tea
description: Black and green tea grown in the Kangra valley since the mid-19th century, known for its colour and flavour. It received a Geographical Indication tag in 2005.
how_to_eat: Drink it plain or lightly sweetened.
how_to_order: Buy packets in Palampur and Dharamshala, or ask for 'Kangra chai' at local tea stalls.

name: Momos
description: Steamed dumplings with vegetable or meat filling, brought by the Tibetan community. They are among the most popular foods in Dharamshala and McLeod Ganj.
how_to_eat: Dip them in the spicy chilli sauce.
how_to_order: Ask for 'veg' or 'chicken momos', steamed or fried, at stalls in McLeod Ganj; usually sold by the plate.

name: Thukpa
description: Tibetan noodle soup with vegetables or meat in a spiced broth, eaten in chilly weather. It is popular in Dharamshala's Tibetan settlement.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot with a spoon and chopsticks.
how_to_order: Ask for 'veg' or 'chicken thukpa' at Tibetan cafés in McLeod Ganj.

name: Tingmo
description: A soft steamed Tibetan bread without filling, twisted for a fluffy texture. In Dharamshala it is served with meat dishes such as shapta.
how_to_eat: Tear it and eat it with a curry or stir-fry.
how_to_order: Ask for tingmo as a side at Tibetan restaurants in McLeod Ganj.

name: Shapta
description: Thinly sliced meat stir-fried with spices and herbs, a Tibetan dish. It is popular in Dharamshala.
how_to_eat: Eat it with tingmo.
how_to_order: Ask for 'shapta' with tingmo at Tibetan restaurants in McLeod Ganj.

name: Bhagsu Cake
description: A layered dessert of chocolate, coconut and caramel, named after the Bhagsunag temple. It is found in cafés around Bhagsu.
how_to_eat: Eat a slice with tea or coffee.
how_to_order: Ask for a slice at cafés in Bhagsu and McLeod Ganj.
